events.title: Sentry error monitoring open-sourced
events.summary: David Cramer open-sourced Sentry in 2010 — an error-tracking service that aggregates exceptions with stack traces and release context.
events.about: Sentry SDKs for Python, JavaScript, Ruby, and dozens of languages piped production errors to a searchable dashboard — grouping duplicates, assigning owners, and linking deploys. It became as standard as Postman for APIs: `SENTRY_DSN` in every startup's environment variables alongside logging and APM.

narrative.whyChosen: Sentry made production exception tracking a default part of the dev stack.
narrative.whyImportant: Grouped stack traces and release tracking cut mean time to diagnose crashes.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams grepped log files manually to find recurring production exceptions.

events.title: BlackBerry Torch released
events.summary: BlackBerry released the BlackBerry Torch — slider phone mixing touch and keyboard on BlackBerry OS 6.
events.about: BlackBerry dominated enterprise mobile before iPhone and Android. Slider phone mixing touch and keyboard on blackberry os 6. BES-connected apps and push email defined mobile workflows for years.

narrative.whyChosen: The BlackBerry Torch was a key BlackBerry hardware milestone.
narrative.whyImportant: BlackBerry hardware set expectations for mobile email and messaging security.
narrative.problemSolved: Business users needed secure mobile email before modern smartphone platforms.
